**Question:** is an unmeasured spectral region the same as an observed absence,
and can partial peak information justify a complete assignment?

Allow **9 minutes**: predict for 2, mask and restore evidence for 4, then audit
two contrasting claims for 3. The molecule does not change when observations
are hidden; all data are fixed simulated U1 teaching observations.

```{=html}
<section class="chem-demo" id="day24" aria-label="Spectral evidence coverage and strength-of-claim challenge">
<p>Enable JavaScript to change available evidence and inspect which claims remain justified.</p>
</section>
<script src="../interactives/core.js"></script>
<script src="../interactives/applications.js"></script>
```

### Predict

The supplied formula is **C₄H₈O₂**. If an IR measurement covers only the
carbonyl window, can you claim that a broad O–H feature was absent? If NMR
supplies only relative integrated areas 3:3:2, can you place an O–CH₂ group
without shifts or splitting?

In the simple NMR model, integration gives H-area ratios while chemical shifts
and multiplicities provide different clues. Missing observations are not
negative observations.

### Explore

1. Begin with the missing-region preset and audit **The O–H absence is observed**.
2. Restore full IR coverage. Identify what new observation now supports or
   challenges the acid candidate.
3. Change NMR from relative areas only to splitting only, then to full evidence.
   Compare **Integrals account for eight H** with **O–CH₂–CH₃ is assigned**.
4. Try the purity and unique-structure claims, even with complete evidence.

### Explain and check

A carbonyl-only window cannot establish O–H absence; the grey area explicitly
marks **unmeasured data**. Reliable relative areas can normalise to 3:3:2 and
account for eight H using the formula, but they do not by themselves locate
those H in the molecule. A 2H quartet near 4.12 ppm with the corresponding
3H triplet provides additional support for O–CH₂–CH₃ in the stated candidate
comparison.

Complete U1 observations favour ethyl ethanoate over the supplied acid and
hydroxyketone alternatives. They do not establish purity or exclude every
conceivable molecular structure.

### Model limits

The coverage choices stipulate which observations are available and whether
O–H detection is adequate. They do not simulate instrumental noise or compute
quantitative confidence probabilities. Use the [local spectroscopy explanations](../spectroscopy/exercise.qmd)
to connect each observation to a structural prediction.
